summary: OpenAI announced price reductions for GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra driven by GPU kernel and speculative-decoding efficiency improvements, introduced a higher-priced Fast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, and upgraded ChatGPT/Codex Auto-review to use Luna.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states specific engineering techniques (GPU kernel improvements, improved speculative decoding) that reduced serving cost and token-generation work per unit, not just a price cut.
mechanisms.quote: 20% lower serving costs through production GPU kernel improvements. More than 15% better token-generation efficiency through improved speculative decoding.

practices.reason: Stated, dated price drops and a faster processing mode change which model/mode is worth using for cost- or latency-sensitive workloads.
practices.quote: GPT-5.6 Luna, the fastest and most affordable model, will cost 80% less.

practices.reason: The described kernel and speculative-decoding improvements are a real efficiency gain but described only as lab-internal results, not a shareable recipe.
practices.quote: 20% lower serving costs through production GPU kernel improvements.

practices.reason: Auto-review's underlying model changed from 5.4 to Luna, altering behavior of an existing agent-review feature that teams relying on it should be aware of.
practices.quote: OpenAI is also upgrading Auto-review in the ChatGPT app and Codex CLI from GPT-5.4 to GPT-5.6 Luna.
